text: When sculpting with wood, sanding is a crucial step to smooth surfaces and remove any imperfections that may arise from cutting, sawing, or shaping the wood. The choice of sandpaper is vital to the finish and the smoothness of the finished piece. Coarse grit sandpaper is ideal for roughing up surfaces to remove chips and debris, while fine grit sandpaper is selected for finer details and smoothing. After the initial sanding to prepare the surface, the wood is often smoothed by using progressively finer sandpaper until it reaches the desired finish. This process ensures that the final piece is not only sculpted but also polished and rendered smooth. While sanding, one must pay close attention to the direction of the grain, as this can affect how the sandpaper interacts with the wood, and consequently the smoothness of the final surface. Properly sanded wood not only enhances the aesthetic appeal but also contributes to the longevity of the finish and the durability of the piece.
summary: Sanding, choose sandpaper, smooth, sawing, shaping.
